Meru
(‘that which throws away [or reflects light]’)
------------------------------------------
Also called Sumeru, this mountain is described as the axis of the whole world. It is golden in colour and is very bright. Its total height is one lakh yojanas—15 lakh kms. or 9 lakh miles since one yojana is 15 kms. or 9 miles—of which 16,000 yojanas (2,40,000 kms. or 1,44,000 miles) are below the earth and 84,000 yojanas (12,60,000 kms. or 7,56,000 miles) above it. It is situated in the centre of the जम्बूद्वीप and भारतवर्ष (India) is to its south.
On its top there is flat plateau of 32,000 yojanas (4,80,00 kms. or 2,88,000 miles). It is here that ब्रह्मा (the creator), his mānasaputras (mind-born sons) like दक्ष, the सप्तर्षिस् like वसिष्ठ live (vide Mahābhārata, Vanaparva 162; Bhāgavata 5.16).
The Kedārnāth mountain (in the Garhwal district of Uttaranchal) is traditionally believed to be the original मेरु.
In a जपमाला (rosary), there is an extra bead fixed perpendicularly to the mālā and above it. This is also called ‘meru’ and is not to be crossed over while doing जप.
